title: Generalized symmetries, invariant solutions and conservation laws in the Jaynes-Cummings model
authors: Luis M. Piñuelas, Pablo C. López Vázquez, Alexander Yakhno
abstract: In this work, we investigate the Jaynes--Cummings model (JCM) using Lie symmetry analysis and conservation-law theory. The dynamics is formulated as a system of partial differential equations by projecting the von Neumann equation onto the atomic degrees of freedom and representing the field mode through its characteristic function. We determine the admitted point and generalized symmetries and construct invariant solutions satisfying the physical conditions imposed by quantum mechanics. The conventional dressed-state dynamics is recovered while a second class of solutions with radial dependence expressed through Heun polynomials is obtained for coupled atom--field configurations.   We also apply the generating functions methodology to derive local conservation laws of the JCM differential system. Besides recovering the conservation of the total number of excitations, we obtain additional conserved currents involving atomic populations, coherence, reduced-state purity, and moments of the field characteristic function. In particular, we derive a balance equation for a combination of atomic purity and coherence whose evolution is controlled by the atom--field coupling and is linked to atom--field correlation and entanglement dynamics. The symmetry structure further generates generalized symmetries and an infinite hierarchy of conservation laws.
summary: This paper applies advanced mathematical techniques, including Lie symmetry analysis and generating functions, to the Jaynes-Cummings model. It successfully derives an infinite set of conservation laws and identifies multiple families of invariant solutions. This provides a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding energy exchange and correlation dynamics in atom-field quantum interactions.
main_problem: The work investigates generalized symmetries, invariant solutions, and conservation laws governing the dynamics of the Jaynes-Cummings model (JCM).
main_result: They derived an infinite hierarchy of conserved currents and found two classes of invariant solutions: one recovering standard dressed-state dynamics and another involving Heun polynomials.
method: The analysis employs Lie symmetry theory, conservation-law methods using generating functions (Vinogradov's framework), and projecting the von Neumann equation onto a characteristic function representation in phase space.
model_or_system: The system is the Jaynes-Cummings model, describing coherent energy exchange between a two-level atom and a single quantized field mode. The dynamics are governed by the von Neumann equation projected into a PDE system in Fourier phase space.
key_observables: Atomic populations ($ho_{ij}$), coherence, reduced-state purity ($P_a$), and moments of the field characteristic function $\mathbf{w}(\vec{r}, t)$.
important_parameters: Detuning ($\Delta$), coupling strength ($g$), and excitation number ($n$). The analysis explores resonant regimes.
main_assumptions: The methodology relies on transforming the dynamics into a PDE system in characteristic function space, allowing for symmetry and conservation law analysis.
paper_structure: The paper systematically applies symmetry analysis to the JCM's governing PDEs. It first establishes conserved currents using generating functions, then solves for invariant solutions by analyzing specific subalgebras ($\Theta_1, \Theta_2$), leading to explicit forms and quantization conditions.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep mathematical characterization of an archetypal quantum optics model (JCM) by finding its underlying symmetries and conservation laws. The discovery of higher-order conserved quantities and novel solution classes is highly valuable for understanding non-trivial dynamics in open quantum systems.
